content: Hi I am new to lean as well as quantum computing. Hope to learn as I hope to do some things at their intersection
Hi! Let us know if you're looking for pointers or places to help out. :)
i was thinking of working on formalizing grover's algorithm in lean. Can you please help me on what I should look at and how should I go through it
I am doing a course on quantum computing at my university and learning lean too

That would be a great thing to do, yeah! There's a few different things that could be meant by "formalizing Grover's algorithm", of course. I think a good goal would be proving that the algorithm given in

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grover%27s_algorithm#Algorithm

has the given success probability. That is, you define that initial state, define the unitary operator U_omega that corresponds to a classical function with unique answer omega, and define the Grover diffusion operator as a unitary operator. Then the theorem would be that you get that

sin⁡2((r+1/2)θ)\sin^2((r+1/2) \theta)sin2((r+1/2)θ)

success probability of getting omega when you measure in the classical basis.

(Extensions would be showing that the the initial superposition, and the Grover diffusion operator, can be efficiently implemented in terms of standard gates; or generalizing the algorithm to where there are $k$ answers to $U_\omega$ instead of just the one. There's also the complementary bound that Grover's algorithm is essentially optimal for black-box oracles, which would be cool to have. These should all come later though!)
Thank you for the kind reply. Will start the work on it and keep on updating here
Great, feel free to ask questions! Quantum computing and Lean are both a bit steep learning curves so I'm happy to help if you feel you're getting blocked on anything. :)
Could I ask you questions related to lean and quantum computing too if I get stuck anywhere??
Sure, right in this channel is fine!

Hi, I am new to Quantuminfo, with baby knowledge in Lean. I am thinking about formalizing Lieb's concavity theorem (saw it on the todo already). But apparently some preliminary notions need to be defined before the proof. I saw the Löwner order is on the repo, so maybe I can start working on defining matrix/operator concave/convex, what do you think?

I also have two worries: (1) although we only care about finite dim Hermitian matrices it seems more straightforward to define operator concavity on the abstract CFC setting (maybe ultimately we will do in someway), (2) (this is Lean-related) I'm not sure if (non)computablity can creates trouble in the future: for example the proof of Jensen looks very computable, very concrete operators and matrix expressions are introduced and manipulated, I need to ensure that any new definitions do make formalizing such proof feasible.

Hi Kevin! Thanks for the interest. :) The second part is easy to answer: noncomputability is not a concern here. A huge amount of Mathlib is already noncomputable. In fact, just asking "is this real number positive or not" is noncomputable; accordingly, anything involving a division of a real number or a logarithm of a real number is necessarily also noncomputable. (Same goes for complex numbers.) In fact it is quite the norm to just start any file with definitions with noncomputable section near the top, and then leave that open for the rest of the file.

As for the first part: yes, in principle all of this can be/should be done in the abstract setting. It does mean you have to think a bit more about your convergence, topology etc. which is why I am sticking with the finite dimensional setting for now. ;) But certainly if you would like to do it in the abstract, that would be great! It also means much likely to get it upstreamed to Mathlib, which is always nice.
I see, thanks Alex! Will get back if I get stuck :D
Great! :D Also feel free to drop comments even if you don't get stuck. I'd like to hear about the progress. :)

Hi and welcome!

I'm glad you're interested in this particular subject, I've done quite a bit of work in that general direction over the past year or so. To get an idea of where we are now, first note that defining operator concavity/convexity/monotonicity is already done, i.e. "f is operator concave" just means that cfc f is concave in the usual sense. Right now we have that a ↦ a^p is operator monotone for p between 0 and 1, and also the log (docs#CFC.monotone_rpow, docs#CFC.log_monotoneOn), and I have some partial progress for operator concavity as well in my private repo, I should just get around to finishing it at some point.

One thing that might be interesting to do right now would be this fairly general theorem on joint operator convexity: Theorem 5.14 in Michael Wolf's lecture notes. I'm pretty sure this can be stated right now using only mathlib.
So glad to know that, thank Frédéric! (Also happy to see Lieb hanging there in Thm 5.15) Will be expecting your progress on operator concavity :D

Frédéric Dupuis said:

and I have some partial progress for operator concavity as well in my private repo

May I assume for the moment that in the future we can see operator concavity/convexity for a ↦ a^p when p is respectively in [0, 1] and [1, 2], also in the most general setting as with the existing monotone_rpow (i.e. [CStarAlgebra A] [PartialOrder A] [StarOrderedRing A])? Mathematically will the new integral representations you are building suffice to deduce it (besides the original matrix case)?
Curious because if so I may want to cast some concavity results on perspective functions in that context too.
Yes, that's the plan!

Update: modulo two sorries, Lieb's concavity together with other new infrastructures are now fully formalized. Meanwhile doing cleanups, refactor and other business, next month I will share my repo and more thoughts.

Briefly: It is first formalized under a more general setup of "H-star Algebra" (a new typeclass): a Hilbert space with a compatible star which acts like adjoint:

 ⟪y,  star x * z⟫ = ⟪x * y, z⟫  = ⟪x,  z * star y⟫

then specializes to n by n complex matrices.
@Alex Meiburg I decided not to base on the Lean-QuantumInfo as different instances are used here.

section HStarAlgebra

variable {H : Type*} [HStarAlgebra ℂ H]
variable [CompleteSpace H] [PartialOrder H] [StarOrderedRing H]
variable [ContinuousFunctionalCalculus ℝ H IsSelfAdjoint] [NonnegSpectrumClass ℝ H]
variable [StarOrderedRing (H →L[ℂ] H)]
/-- **Lieb's Concavity Theorem** for general operators:
Special case of `LiebExtension` with `p = 1 - s`, `q = s`. -/
theorem LiebConcavity {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s ∧ s < 1) (x : H) :
    ConcaveOn ℝ {(A, B) : H × H | IsStrictlyPositive A ∧ 0 ≤ B}
        (fun (A, B) => re ⟪x, A ^ s * x * B ^ (1 - s)⟫_ℂ) :=
  LiebExtension (by linarith) hs.1 (by linarith) x

end HStarAlgebra

--- the packed frobenius-normed related instances on Matrix n n ℂ
open FrobeniusMat

variable {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

local notation "M[" n "]" => Matrix n n ℂ

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- **Lieb's Concavity Theorem** for matrices [Nik2013, Thm 1.2(a)]:
`(A, B) ↦ re ((A ^ s * K * B ^ (1 - s) * Kᴴ).trace)` is jointly concave in `(A, B)`
for `0 < s < 1`, `A` positive definite and `B` positive semidefinite -/
theorem LiebConcavity_matrix {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s ∧ s < 1) (K : M[n]) :
    ConcaveOn ℝ {(A, B) : M[n] × M[n] | A.PosDef ∧ B.PosSemidef}
      (fun (A, B) => re ((A ^ s * K * B ^ (1 - s) * Kᴴ).trace)) := by
  convert LiebConcavity hs K using 1
  simp_rw [isStrictlyPositive_iff_posDef, nonneg_iff_posSemidef]

The two sorries are:

  1. For commuting elements in a CStarAlgebra, (a * b) ^ r = a ^ r * b ^ r for any (positive) real r. It seems very nontrivial to formalize, but it is not a substantial sorry as it only affects simp of expressions with power.
  2. Operator concavity/convexity for a \mapsto a ^ p . This is an ongoing work by @Frédéric Dupuis .

Main references:

  • "Simplest" proof of Lieb
  • Perspectives of matrix convex functions
  • Jensen Operator Convexity in C* algebra

I'm looking forward to seeing the code! That second sorry will land in mathlib fairly soon I think. For the first one, I think it should be reasonably easy to formalise using the material in Mathlib.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.Commute.
This sounds great! We've recently finished (a sufficiently general version of) DPI modulo Lieb's concavity, so this makes me extra happy. :)

For commuting elements in a CStarAlgebra, (a * b) ^ r = a ^ r * b ^ r for any (positive) real r. It seems very nontrivial to formalize, but it is not a substantial sorry as it only affects simp of expressions with power.

I have a proof of this for matrices, at least. (It's the straightforward argument of, if they commute we can simultanteously diagonalize -> prove it for diagonal matrices.)

Right.Mathlib.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.Commute is very stare at the moment, . The proof should be in the same spirit with diagonalisation, except here we will need to take the comm subalgebra generated by a and b and extract the hom from the function algebra over the joint spectrum σ(a, b) to it, but that ultimately depends on some multivariate CFC?

A summative note and personal reflection: this is my first time working on a non-toy formalisation task, so it has many rooms of improvements and for the best not be used externally (afterall, there has been a version of Lieb integrated to the Lean-QuantumInfo anyway). Here is the project website built by this blueprint tool.

Lean indeed has a super steep learning curve! Besides the theorem-proving aspect, i have tried very hard fighting with diamond issues, transparency issues, understanding how elaborator works in relation to the behaviours of tactics and type class inference system, etc. All in all it is an rewarding process, I have enjoyed defining and developing new abstraction layers, learning to declare and scoped instances appropriately, trying to catch up the Mathlib standard. I am thinking take formalisation as a personal hobby!

Finally I'd like to thank you guys @Alex Meiburg @Frédéric Dupuis having conversations on the chat with encouragements!
